market_holds: Spot $49.375 at the 18:10 UTC seal, $49.69 intraday on Yahoo bars. The stock is up 15.1% over 5 days and 17.7% over 20, and about 25% off its $39.60 close on 2026-10-14. It is still about 18% below its high near $60 before approval, and it fell from $55.41 to $46.65 in the week after the 2026-09-11 FDA approval (Yahoo chart v8). The options price an event move of 11.2% (straddle 12.6% to the 11-20 expiry, ATM IV 86%) with a 28 vol-point put skew, so downside is paid for, but the ATM spread is 55% of mid, so the options read is only indicative (sealed baseline). The last 8 prints moved a median 3.1%; the big ones were catalyst quarters (+24.4% in Nov-2025 on the resubmission path, +10% in Aug-2026). Consensus for Q3 is about $260k revenue and a loss of -$0.87 (Earnings Whispers preview via Finviz, 2026-11-03), and Benzinga shows $70k Q3 and $5.4M Q4. FY26 is about $5.3M and FY27 about $133M (Visible Alpha via the Stocktwits/S&P coverage of 2026-09-14). So revenue is not the line. The line is launch-throughput language: enrollment or start forms, prescribers, prior-authorization approvals, time to first infusion. Management itself warned of early PA denials and more than 60 days from prescription to infusion over the first six months (same preview), which keeps the bar low. There is no numeric guidance. Cash was $492.1M on 2026-06-30 against about $110M of quarterly opex, the ATM was used in Q2 ($63M), and a new ATM supplement was filed 2026-08-06. A PRV ($100-200M) is planned for sale and no sale has been reported. Public signal already out: a director (Samsara BioCapital) bought 289,470 shares, about $12.0M at $41.3-41.8, on Oct 23 and 26, filed 2026-10-27, and the stock has risen about 19% since.
view: This is Scholar Rock's first print as a commercial company, and it covers about three weeks of launch after the 2026-09-11 approval of ISEMBYLD. Q3 revenue will be near zero, consistent with the company's own warning of a 60+ day path from prescription to infusion, and consensus already sits at a few hundred thousand dollars. So the reaction will be decided by whatever early-demand metric management chooses to disclose (start or enrollment forms, prescriber breadth, payer policies), by Q3 cash and ATM usage, and by any PRV sale or EU/SRK439 timing news. Two forces pull opposite ways. In favour of a good print: a director's $12M open-market buy in late October, during what is normally a pre-earnings blackout, suggests the board saw nothing alarming in early launch data. Payer policies are appearing (BCBSM, Blue Shield CA effective 11-01, Centene preemptive policies). Rare-disease companies usually disclose start-form counts when they flatter. Against: the stock has already rerated about 25% off its mid-October low and 15% in the last week, partly with a biotech tape (XBI about +5% over the same days). The insider buy is public and has visibly been traded on. An early-launch print with qualitative metrics and a quarter of ATM dilution is a classic sell-the-news setup after a run-up, and the options market pays for downside. I can find no fresh, independent read on demand (no community, payer-count or script data) that the market lacks. Net, I cannot tell the direction, and I expect a move somewhat below the implied 11%.

recommendation.reason: The line is the early-launch demand metric, and I found no public trace of it (no patient-community, script or start-form data) that the price lacks. The one positive signal, a $12M director purchase at about $41, is public and the stock has risen about 19% since it was filed. The run-up into a print with immaterial revenue offsets it. No mechanism clears the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A disclosed start/enrollment-form count well above the market's informal expectation (several hundred patients in the first seven weeks) or a PRV sale near $150M+ would make this an up print. A vague qualitative launch update plus heavy Q3 ATM issuance would make it a down print.

key_evidence.shows: FDA approved ISEMBYLD on 2026-09-11 for SMA patients aged 2+ who are on SMN2 therapy, so Q3 holds about three weeks of launch.
Director (Samsara) bought 289,470 shares, about $12.0M, at $41.31-41.82 on Oct 23 and 26, before the Q3 print. Public since Oct 27.
Consensus Q3 revenue about $260k, EPS -$0.87. Management expects early PA denials and 60+ days from Rx to infusion. Analysts are watching prescriber enrollment and payer coverage.
Price $310k/yr. 6,600 eligible US patients. Cash $492M plus $150M debt. Plans to sell the PRV and no equity raise intended. Raymond James warned much of the launch is priced in.
Low close $39.60 on 10-14, then a rally to about $49.7. +15% in the 5 days into the print while XBI rose about 5%.
Payer policies are being written. Blue Shield CA commercial is effective 11-01 but still has placeholder criteria, and Centene's preemptive policy excludes prior Zolgensma.
New ATM prospectus supplement filed 2026-08-06, so Q3 share issuance is possible and will show in the 10-Q.

self_critique: The case for long: the director bought $12M at $41 inside the quarter, which rarely happens without strong early-demand visibility. Rare-disease launches that disclose start forms in their first print often surprise up, because sell-side models assume a slow PA-gated ramp. The heavy put skew also means positioning is defensive, so a decent update could squeeze. The case for short: a 25% rebound and 15% in five days into a quarter with no revenue, an ATM likely tapped, and the fact that 'launch going well' adjectives rarely add value at the open. I cannot separate these with public evidence.
approach_notes: P4 (prove 'priced in') helped me frame the insider buy as a public signal the price has already reacted to. P3's stakeholder and community routes turned up nothing for a three-week-old rare-disease launch. For first-launch quarters, the playbook could say that the disclosed demand metric is unknowable in advance and that the run-up versus a low company-set bar is the main read.
